source_context: non-urban air or from high stacks
default_context_mappings.comment: `non-urban air or from high stacks` names two situations at once -- a release in the countryside, or a release from a tall stack anywhere -- and no context can hold both. It was published as envi-air-hist15me, which says a dairy barn's ammonia left a 150-metre chimney; the other reading, Ground level + Rural, says a power-station plume was released at head height, and nothing in a flow says which it is. EF 3.1's factors settle it, and they pick neither: in all 40 (flow, method) pairs where this compartment and one of EF's narrow non-urban compartments are both characterised, EF gives this one exactly the factor it gives `Emissions to non-urban air high stack` -- particles (PM2.5) 3.01757e-06, against 1.13763e-05 non-urban close to ground and 1.62949e-06 non-urban very high stack. That compartment is envi-air-mest15me-ru10pesq here, so this keeps the rural qualifier the compartment does assert and takes the stack height EF characterises rather than the one the name suggests. What is given up: a release that really did leave a >150-metre stack is published as a sub-150-metre one, which EF's own numbers say is the smaller error. Decided once for the three lists that spell this compartment differently -- EF 3.1, ecoinvent in all five versions, and BAFU's `emissions to air / low. pop.`, SimaPro's spelling of ecoinvent v2's `low population density` -- because moving one alone would split them apart. (#79)

Was envi-air-grle-unkn, which asserted a stratum the source does not name. ecoinvent's `unspecified` says only that the release went to air; reading it as ground level split it from EF 3.1's `Emissions to air, unspecified` and BAFU's `emissions to air / unspecified`, which both sit on envi-air-unkn -- one compartment under three spellings landing in two places. It split ecoinvent from itself as well: the rows the correspondence tables match onto EF's unspecified air flow (383 in 3.8 up to 1,175 in 3.12) were already published in envi-air-unkn, with the guard reconciling that by a permitted coarsening in correspondence-context-routing.json, and only the rows that found no EF partner stayed behind. On the 2026-08-13 build those were all 54 flows in envi-air-grle-unkn -- every one an ecoinvent creation, none carrying a characterisation factor, in a context no other list can reach. The coarsening entry is removed with this change. Nothing is given up: the ground-level qualifier was never in the source. (#79)

ecoinvent's one water compartment that names its body -- EF 3.1 gives all six of its water bodies one compartment, so the rest need a per-flow rule. The subcompartment holds exactly one flow, `Water, unspecified natural origin` 2caa889e, in every version 3.8 to 3.12. ecoinvent publishes no definition of `fossil well`, and the name reads either as a well into a fossil aquifer or as a fossil-fuel well producing formation water -- but those converge on this body rather than diverging. Produced water from a hydrocarbon well is connate water in a confined formation with negligible modern recharge, which is fossil groundwater; the two readings differ in why somebody drilled, not in what the water is, and this axis is the body. Salinity does not argue against it either: formation water is typically hypersaline, and salinity is a material property carried on the other axis. ecoinvent's own correspondence table sends this flow to EF 3.1's `ground water`, so they read it as groundwater too; `Confined aquifer with fossil groundwater` is the more precise version of what they said. The emission side already maps `water / fossil well` here, and this makes the two sides agree. Repointed in all five registered versions at once: the subcompartment is unchanged between them. See #263.

Was envi-wate-unkn, the same IRI as `Emissions to water, unspecified`, so EF's 7,186 long-term water flows collapsed onto the short-term ones under deduplication. That collapse is what stranded ecoinvent's `water / ground-, long-term`: its correspondence table points 260 of 269 rows at EF's own long-term flow, and following the deprecation redirect landed them back on unspecified water, where 180 of them received a short-term factor for a release ecoinvent defines as >100 years out. This is the same move #40 made for `Emissions to air, unspecified (long-term)`, and for the same reason -- both sides of a temporal pair have to meet in the temporal context or neither does. The previous comment read `Temporal differentiation belongs to LCIA, not LCI`, which was decided before ecoinvent's row moved; #41 is where the combination was weighed. It costs ~7,156 uncharacterised identifiers: only 30 of the 7,186 carry any EF 3.1 factor, so almost nothing is recovered by publishing them, and what is bought is that no flow silently inherits a factor from a different compartment.

The `/kg` was BAFU writing the unit into the name (#67) and is off the row by the time this rule is read -- #78 carries the row in cubic metres at 1000 kg/m3 with the density stated, and bafu-2026-v1-manual-fixes.json renames it. This comment used to argue that the suffix should stay, on the ground that the mass and volume spellings are not one resource measured two ways. That was never a question a name could answer: a flow's identity is its substance and its context, `(flow_object_id, context_iri)` is unique, and the unit is not in it -- so the two rows have reached one flow in this compartment since BAFU was first merged, and the suffix was keeping two names apart above a single flow. The archive says reading them as one costs almost nothing here: 64 datasets use each spelling in this compartment and 63 use both, and the mass is 6.58e-05 to 6.65e-05 of what the volume implies, a ratio too tight across 63 datasets to be two independent measurements. Both rows are kept, each with its own identifier and its own mapping back to BAFU, because dropping either would lose an inventory a process uses. (#83, #67)

The volume-measured half of the row above, and the same reasoning about the compartment.

It keeps the vendor's own name rather than being renamed to `Water, unspecified natural origin` the way the `resources / in water` row of that name is: 63 datasets carry this row beside that one, so a dataset that named both would be naming one flow twice. (#83, #67)

This one is not: `unspecified` is the absence of a statement about where the water came from, not a statement that it came out of the ground.

The vendor settles it. 81 rows of this list carry this exact name in `resources / in water` and reach EF 3.1's water withdrawal from an unstated body; this row differs from all 81 in nothing but the compartment. The same water with `process,` in the middle of its name, which says what the water is for rather than what it is -- a fact about the dataset using it, not about the substance. Same compartment, same reading, same destination as the row above and as its own `resources / land` sibling. (#83, #67)

Waste heat is released into the air, never taken out of it. The name is corrected in bafu-2026-v1-manual-fixes.json to the one the vendor uses for the same flow everywhere else; the two are halves of one correction. (#75, #4)

The same standing timber, and the same reading, from the third compartment BAFU files it in. `resources / unspecified` has no context of its own -- the compartment rule sends it to ground resources, which is where most of BAFU's unspecified rows belong -- so this row was landing in `Resource / Ground` while the rows from `resources / land` and `resources / biotic` both landed in `Resource / Biotic`. (#67, #4)

flow_specific_context_mappings.source_name: Energy, gross calorific value, in biomass, resource correction
flow_specific_context_mappings.comment:
The energy in a tree, credited back from the compartment BAFU leaves blank. A resource correction is not a thing in its own right: it is an amount of a resource written with the opposite sign, so it does its work only if it lands on the same flow as the extraction it cancels (#294). Nine of BAFU's ten corrections do. This one did not, because it is the only one the vendor files in two compartments -- `resources / biotic`, 51 exchanges, and `resources / unspecified`, 21, every one of the 72 negative. The biotic row reaches EF 3.1's own `biomass` flow, which ecoinvent 3.8, ecoinvent 3.12 and BAFU's own biotic rows all share; the unspecified row followed the compartment rule into `Resource / Ground`, where biomass had no flow at all, so the merge minted one for it. One accounting entry published in two places, and the half that landed in the ground has nothing beside it to cancel.

`unspecified` is not a statement that the energy came out of the ground -- it is the absence of a statement, which is what the compartment rule's own comment says of it. The energy in a tree is a biotic resource whichever compartment the row was filed in: the same reading the standing-timber rows above are given, and the same one the geothermal row below is given in reverse. The archive settles it. None of the 21 datasets carrying this row carries any other biomass row, so the amount it credits was charged in some other dataset, on the biotic flow -- which is the flow it now reaches.

It moves alone. BAFU files the resource itself in three compartments too -- 394 exchanges under `biotic`, 19 under `unspecified`, 7 under `in air` -- and those two strays are #89's question rather than this one's, so the ground flow stays published until they are settled. Neither flow carries a characterisation factor, so no published number moves. (#69, #294)

Heat drawn from the rock beneath, which is a ground resource wherever the row was filed: biotic means living, or made by something living, and nothing about geothermal heat is. BAFU files the name in two compartments -- `resources / in ground` in 57 datasets of the 11,947 in the 2026 v1 release, `resources / biotic` in 5 -- and the compartment rule believed both, so one energy carrier was published as two flows on one substance: EF 3.1, ecoinvent 3.8 and ecoinvent 3.12 all reach the ground one, and the biotic row minted a second flow beside it with no characterisation on it. This is the same reading, and the same fix, as the standing-timber rows below, which go the other way: what a resource is decides its compartment, not which compartment the vendor happened to file each row in. All five of the biotic datasets carry the in-ground row as well, at one to two orders of magnitude more energy and never the same number, so the two rows are separate amounts of one resource rather than one amount written twice, and summing them onto one flow counts nothing twice. (#87)

Cooling water of no stated origin, which is water taken from the environment and not out of the ground. BAFU ships eight rows under this name, all in cubic metres: seven are filed in `resources / in water` and reach EF 3.1's `Water to Cooling` -- published as `Cooling water` in `Resource / Water`, carrying 209 characterisation factors -- and this one, the RER row, is filed in `resources / in ground`. The name argues against that compartment: `unspecified natural origin` is the vendor saying it does not record where the water came from, which is the opposite of stating that it came out of the ground. Two more things say the same. BAFU already ships a second RER row under this name in `resources / in water`, so the ground filing is not the one place RER cooling water is recorded; and the seven siblings all carry water's registry number 7732-18-5 while this row carries none, which is what a row entered on its own looks like. Left to the compartment rule it reached `Resource / Ground`, where the list has no cooling-water flow, so the merge minted one: `Cooling water` taken from the ground, with no factor under any method, and an inventory using it scored nothing for water its seven siblings are fully characterised for. Same reading as the geothermal row above and the helium row below -- what the resource is decides where it is filed, not which compartment one row happened to land in. (#117)

Helium is taken out of the ground, not out of the air. EF 3.1 files it with the gases that are recovered from air by cryogenic separation -- `Renewable element resources from air` holds nine flows, and the other eight are dinitrogen, oxygen, argon, Argon-40, neon, krypton, xenon and radon -- and helium is the one member of that compartment nobody separates from air. At 5.2 ppm it is too dilute to be worth recovering; commercial helium comes from natural gas deposits, where it reaches a few per cent, and that is what an inventory using this flow is accounting for.

`Renewable` is wrong for the same reason and in the same direction. Atmospheric helium is not replenished on any human timescale -- it is light enough to escape the atmosphere, and what is in the crust arrives from the alpha decay of uranium and thorium over geological time -- so the compartment claims twice over that this is a gas the air keeps making. `Resource -> Ground` is the consensus context the other non-renewable elements from ground already use.

ecoinvent 3.12 says the same thing in its own data, and that is what makes this a disagreement rather than a reading: its flow is `Helium, in natural gas`, CAS 7440-59-7, in `natural resource / in ground`. Because the two compartments contradict, the merge could not put that row on EF's flow and minted a second one instead, so the published list held helium as a resource in two places -- which is what `substance-in-two-places` reports, and what the queue's own note says to answer with a rule here (#114).

Nothing is recharacterised by the move: neither flow carries a characterisation factor in either implementation of EF 3.1, and no method this project publishes scores a helium resource at all.

Process water drawn from nature, filed in the ground. `unspecified natural origin` is BAFU saying it does not record where the water came from, which is the opposite of stating that it came out of the ground -- the reading #117 gave the cooling-water row in this compartment, and the one its own siblings already get: this row's four siblings under this name, in `resources / land` (64 datasets), `resources / unspecified` (64) and `resources / in water` (7), all reach EF 3.1's water withdrawal and its 209 characterisation factors, and the `land` and `unspecified` pairs were sent there by #83's rules above. This one, 60 datasets, reached a minted `Groundwater` in `Resource / Ground` carrying none. The archive settles it: in 54 of those 60 datasets the land and unspecified rows appear beside this one, so BAFU is writing one withdrawal twice in one dataset rather than describing two. Green water is rainfall held in soil and used by plants. EF 3.1 files it as a resource taken from air, because precipitation is how it arrives; ecoinvent 3.12 files it in the ground, because that is where a plant's roots reach it. flow_specific_context_mappings.source_name: Carbon dioxide in air, as CO2e (GWP aggr timing)
flow_specific_context_mappings.comment: Not a substance flow. Its amount is already a characterisation result: the method gives it -1 in `Global warming, fossil` regardless of what was taken up, where a real uptake would carry the substance's own factor. `GWP aggr timing` says the emission's timing profile was aggregated into that result upstream.
